title: Dutch Roll
description: A Dutch roll rotates the camera around the lens axis over time, so a level horizon becomes a canted one. Unease arrives as a move, not as a frozen Dutch still.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The world itself tilts while we watch. Rank, gravity, and architecture go off their contract in duration rather than in a single locked cant.

You can stop on a Dutch angle, but the technique is the roll that got you there. It is the wrong tool when the floor is already the story (a listing ship), and the wrong tool if you needed a full continuous spin until up is gone.
A slow roll into a cant is not a revolving corridor.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Rotate around the optical axis (roll), usually from a locked nodal point. Keep pan and tilt still unless you combine on purpose.
End on a readable Dutch or return to level when the character finds the floor. Prompt a slow roll on the lens axis, horizon rotating from level into a Dutch angle.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for unease that arrives in time, not as a still cant. Concrete beat: a level street, then the horizon slowly dies as a fever starts.
Do not start already tilted if the arrival is the point.

blocks.text: A Dutch Angle is a still cant. A Camera Roll continues until gravity is optional, or uses a rotating set.
Dutch roll is the timed transition on the roll axis into (or out of) a Dutch. Do not confuse it with terrain incline.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a locked Dutch Angle or a full Camera Roll. The tell is a still tilt from frame one, or a continuous spin past 45 degrees with no stop.
The fix: start level, roll on axis over time, end on a chosen cant.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Dutch Roll in film?
It is a camera roll around the lens axis over time, turning a level horizon into a Dutch angle (or the reverse) as a move.
Dutch Roll vs Dutch Angle
A Dutch angle is a still canted frame. Dutch roll is the motion that creates or releases that cant.
When should I use Dutch Roll?
When unease should arrive in duration. Do not use it if you only needed a locked cant, or a full gravity-free spin.
How do I prompt Dutch Roll for AI image or video?
Write camera slowly rolls on its lens axis, horizon from level into a Dutch angle around [Subject]. No pan, no full 360 roll unless you change technique.
